prompt: fastify.addHttpMethod silently overrides a method that already exists, such as addHttpMethod('GET', { hasBody: true }). Deprecate implicit overrides: addHttpMethod accepts a new option overrideExisting (default false). When the method already exists (as a method with or without a body) and overrideExisting is not true, emit a new Fastify deprecation warning FSTDEP025 (defined with the other warnings in lib/warnings.js, name 'FastifyDeprecation', code 'FSTDEP025', message 'Calling addHttpMethod for existing method "%s" without { overrideExisting: true } is deprecated. In Fastify v6, this will throw an error.' with the method name), every time this happens, not only the first time. With { overrideExisting: true } no warning is emitted, and adding a method that does not exist yet emits no warning. The override itself still takes effect in both cases (for example, GET then accepts a body).
requirement: addHttpMethod(method, { hasBody = false, overrideExisting = false }): when method is already in the bodyless or bodywith set and overrideExisting is not true, FSTDEP025 is emitted via process-warning with unlimited: true (name 'FastifyDeprecation', code 'FSTDEP025', message with %s = method). overrideExisting: true suppresses it; a new method never warns; the hasBody change is applied either way.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: addHttpMethod('GET', { hasBody: true }) emits a warning named 'FastifyDeprecation' with code 'FSTDEP025' and message 'Calling addHttpMethod for existing method "GET" without { overrideExisting: true } is deprecated. In Fastify v6, this will throw an error.'
the warning is emitted on every such call, not only the first
{ overrideExisting: true } emits no warning, and adding a method that does not exist yet emits no warning
with { hasBody: true, overrideExisting: true }, a GET route with a body schema receives and returns the JSON body

adjudication_rules: Score pass only if every hidden check passes. No partial credit.

The reference is that change applied to v5.11.0 (runtime only; docs and types not graded). The hidden suite follows the upstream tests and adds the every-time and new-method cases the prompt states.
